t: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to Denial of Service via temporary file leak after client disconnect
d: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 3.0.0 through 10.1.3, temporary files written by the saveRequestFiles helper are removed only by a response hook that runs when the response finishes or errors. When a client completes an upload and then disconnects before the handler writes the reply, for example while the handler scans, hashes or forwards the file, the response only emits a close event, the cleanup hook never runs, and the saved files are left on disk. An unauthenticated client can repeat this cheaply to exhaust disk space and deny service to applications that save uploaded files to disk. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.4, and users should upgrade to 10.1.4 or later. As a workaround, avoid saving request files for untrusted clients, or clean the saved files from a close handler on the raw response so removal also happens when the client disconnects.

t: @fastify/proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via ignored IPv6 zone identifier
d: @fastify/proxy-addr determines which network hops are trusted proxies and backs Fastify's trustProxy setting, so that forwarded headers can be believed. In versions 3.0.0 through 5.1.2, when trustProxy is configured with a zoned IPv6 link-local address, the trust comparison checks only the address bits and ignores the zone identifier, so a host on another link of a multi-homed server that carries the same link-local address is trusted as well. Such an attacker can spoof the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers, making the client IP, host and protocol reported by Fastify attacker-chosen values and defeating IP allowlists, rate limiting and audit logging. Exploitation requires a multi-homed server whose trustProxy is a zoned link-local address and an attacker directly on one of its other links; the default configuration and global, private or loopback trust entries are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/proxy-addr 5.1.3, and users should upgrade to 5.1.3 or later. As a workaround, avoid trusting a zoned link-local address on a multi-homed host and trust a global, private or loopback proxy address instead.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the cinema report generator. An authenticated attacker with an admin privileges can supply an invalid date_from value causing the application to return a detailed error page that discloses the full SELECT statement (table and column names, JOIN, GROUP BY and ORDER BY clauses, bind parameter placeholders) and a PHP DateTime parsing exception. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Exposure of KSeF API Integration Secret in visualTicket
d: visualTicket displays secret token value in admin settings panel. The "KSeF - Token API" edit form renders a pre-filled field containing the actual KSeF API integration secret without any masking. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket exposes sensitive information in error messages in the administrative report generator. Because application exception details and SQL queries are rendered in the HTTP response in the production environment, an authenticated administrator submitting an invalid date_from value in the report request receives a detailed error page disclosing the full SELECT statement, table and column names, JOINs, bind parameters, and a PHP DateTime exception. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Missing Authorization in visualTicket
d: visualTicket does not require authentication for the PDF invoice file serving functionality. Invoice PDF files reside in a web-accessible static path without a session check, while authorization is enforced only at the invoice registry page. A remote unauthenticated attacker who obtains the URL of an invoice PDF can download the document without authorization. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the selectedDate parameter in the order summary page. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Cross-Site Request Forgery in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) across multiple endpoints. State-changing operations are exposed via GET requests without any CSRF protection. A remote attacker can persuade an authenticated user (including administrator) into navigating to a prepared URL, causing the victim's browser to issue requests that carry the active session cookie and perform unintended actions. This issue was partially addressed in version 20260817: settings changes and bulk refunds require POST with a CSRF token, and the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which limits cross-site requests.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the JSONP callback parameter. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure via JSONP in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through JSONP on session-bound cart service endpoints. Session-bound data (including the session id, cart id, item ids, ticket/event metadata, quantities and prices) is returned inside a script wrapper, and since the symfony session token can also be passed in the URL, a remote attacker who obtains the token can read the cart session token and cart data. This issue was mitigated in version 20260817: the session cookie is set with SameSite=Lax, which prevents other websites from reading cart data of the victim’s session.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in logon functionality. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Session Fixation in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Session Fixation via the symfony session identifier passed in the URL. The application accepts the symfony session ID from the query string and set it as a session cookie in the HTTP response, allowing the browser's active session to be overwritten. This behaviour enables an attacker to fix a session ID for a victim and later hijack the authenticated session. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Reflected XSS in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the "culture" and "sf_culture" parameters. An attacker can prepare a specially crafted URL that, when opened, results in arbitrary JavaScript execution in the error page in the victim's browser. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Information Exposure Through Error Message in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to information exposure through an error message in the order creation functionality. Because detailed data-layer exceptions are returned to the client instead of being logged server-side only, a remote unauthenticated attacker can submit a valid checkout request with an invalid payment_type value, causing the application to return a detailed SQL/ORM error that discloses the database name, table and column names, query structure, and foreign key constraint name. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Path Traversal in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the thumbnail generation mechanism. The file parameter is used directly when constructing the output filesystem path without restriction to the uploads directory, allowing a remote attacker to use ../ sequences to escape /uploads/user_temp_images/ and write the generated JPEG file to other writable locations, including the web root. This allows unauthorized creation of JPEG files outside the intended uploads directory, leading to file-space pollution and potential overwriting of predictable resources with matching names. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Insecure Direct Object Reference in visualTicket
d: visualTicket is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in the cart service. The server modifies or deletes a cart item based solely on the supplied "cart_id" without checking whether the object belongs to the current symfony session. Cart identifiers are created sequentially and allows prediction of valid values. An attacker holding an independent session can reference another user's "cart_id" and change its state, for example altering the quantity or deleting the item. This allows modification or deletion of items in another user's cart, alteration of the cart total, and disruption of the reservation/purchase process. This issue was fixed in version 20260817.

t: Remote Code Execution in Batflat CMS
d: Batflat CMS does not sanitize data passed to the /contact endpoint. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a POST request with a crafted message, causing arbitrary PHP code execution with www-data user privileges. The project is no longer maintained and the issue has not been fixed.

t: Netskope Client and Endpoint DLP Local Privilege Escalation via Insecure OpenSSL Configuration
d: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Privilege Escalation via /kal-api/auth/user/edit
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify any account via the /kal-api/auth/user/edit endpoint. Attackers holding only read permission can set their admin flag and 'all' permission or reset an administrator's password to fully take over the instance.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Git Credential Disclosure via Documentation API
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated read-only users to retrieve Git deployment credentials via documentation API responses. Attackers can query GET /kal-api/docs/documentations or POST /kal-api/docs/documentation to obtain plaintext gitUser and gitPassword values and authenticate to external Git repositories.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Stored XSS via Unrestricted File Upload
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows read-only authenticated users to upload HTML or SVG files via the upload-file endpoint without type restrictions. Attackers can share links to files served unauthenticated through the file get route, executing JavaScript in the admin origin to steal administrator JWTs from localStorage.

t: Kalmia through 0.2.0 Authentication Bypass via viewToken Cookie
d: Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in RsPressMiddleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private documentation by supplying any non-empty viewToken cookie. Attackers can send requests with a forged viewToken cookie, which is never validated as a JWT, to read all pages and assets of RequireAuth documentation sites.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Unauthenticated File Upload via @tensei/media files/upload
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the @tensei/media plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload dangerous file types via the files/upload route. Attackers can set the multipart Content-Type to upload HTML or SVG files served from the application origin, causing stored cross-site scripting and storage consumption.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Unauthenticated Prototype Pollution via sort Parameter
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in parseSortFromStringToObject of @tensei/rest that allows unauthenticated attackers to set Object.prototype properties via the sort parameter. Attackers can send a sort value like __proto__.<name>:<value> to list, fetch-one, update or delete routes before authorization, altering application logic and causing denial of service.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Privilege Escalation via Self-Assigned Roles in @tensei/auth
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in @tensei/auth that allows unauthenticated or authenticated users to assign themselves arbitrary roles via the exposed User Roles field. Attackers can supply a roles array during registration, a POST to the users route, or a PATCH to their own record to gain administrator permissions.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Authentication Bypass via Hard-Coded JWT Secret in @tensei/auth
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in @tensei/auth that falls back to the hard-coded JWT signing key 'auth-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset. Unauthenticated attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary user ids accepted by populateContextFromToken to impersonate any user, including administrators.

t: Tensei through 0.11.5 Open Redirect via @tensei/social-auth OAuth Callback
d: Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the @tensei/social-auth SocialAuthCallbackController that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying an unvalidated clientCallback query parameter. Attackers can craft links to the /:provider/callback route that send victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing and leak the issued temporary access token appended after login.

t: Insecure deserializaiton in the httpx Ruby gem via unsafe Oj object-mode
d: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

t: Denial of service in Mattermost Desktop via crafted file download

t: udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block() When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash like: Oops: general protection fault KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503) Call Trace: vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419) do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583) __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602) This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being treated as a folio pointer with obvious results. Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either 0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

t: nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners() client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners() nfsd4_exchange_id nfsd4_proc_compound nfsd_dispatch svc_process Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner list.

t: ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc() When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed, Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd. unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset); int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset; if (!dacl_offset || (dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size)) goto out; Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check") fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out, because it is only valid for 32-bit builds. Reproduced on 32-bit ARM with KASAN, by a client sending SMB2 SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the same file: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105) Read of size 2 at addr c2a273fa by task kworker/1:1/35 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 35 Comm: kworker/1:1 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc2+ #5 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work Call trace: kasan_check_range from build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105) build_sec_desc from smb2_query_info (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:7676) smb2_query_info from handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:160) handle_ksmbd_work from process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3401) process_one_work from worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3473) worker_thread from kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436) Add overflow check.

t: usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512. The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c ("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means. But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to 1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this. As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

t: ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes). A malicious MDS can declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so nothing downstream rejects the reply. ceph_fill_trace() -> update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front. Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling parse_reply_info_dir(). A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10 bytes. BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in __update_dentry_lease.constprop.0 (fs/ceph/inode.c:1459) Read of size 4 at addr ffff888026c63d65 by task kworker/0:3/2366 Workqueue: ceph-msgr ceph_con_workfn Call Trace: __update_dentry_lease.constprop.0 (fs/ceph/inode.c:1459) ceph_fill_trace (fs/ceph/inode.c:1474 fs/ceph/inode.c:1823) mds_dispatch (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4229 fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7225) ceph_con_process_message (net/ceph/messenger.c:1424) ceph_con_v1_try_read (net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:1430) ceph_con_workfn (net/ceph/messenger.c:1576) process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396) worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560) kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436) ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158) ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245) The buggy address is located 357 bytes inside of allocated 360-byte region [ffff888026c63c00, ffff888026c63d68)

t: ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire: ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then overwrites it with the size of the "in" set. Neither is bounded by CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[]. The clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally bounded by mdsc->max_sessions. The map arrives on the monitor connection, which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode. CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt. Reject it where the rank space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map(). t: ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps + num_prior_parent_snaps). t: virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work virtio-net uses a boolean to gate rx_mode_work during device teardown. The flag is changed under RTNL, but ndo_set_rx_mode checks it under the address-list lock. A callback can therefore pass the check and enqueue work after teardown has flushed it. The work is also enabled before late probe operations that can fail, allowing probe unwind to free the netdev with work still queued. t: libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len handle_command_ack() bounds the decode with msg->front_alloc_len, the size of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the monitor sent. mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to get_generic_reply(), which returns the preallocated ->reply of whichever generic request carries the same tid, so the buffer keeps its fixed size however short the reply is. An ack with hdr.front_len below sizeof(struct ceph_mon_request_header) + sizeof(u32), including 0, still passes ceph_decode_need(), and ceph_decode_32() returns four bytes that were never received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and is then rejected. The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not flag it. req->result reaches userspace through ceph_monc_do_statfs(), ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes it to ERR_PTR() unchecked, which faults: rbd: failed to get latest osdmap: -186318427 BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfffe9ca034 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI RIP: 0010:do_rbd_add (drivers/block/rbd.c:7105) Call Trace: ... kernfs_fop_write_iter (fs/kernfs/file.c:345) vfs_write (fs/read_write.c:595 fs/read_write.c:687) ksys_write (fs/read_write.c:739) do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84) entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121) Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception Use msg->front.iov_len, matching handle_subscribe_ack(), handle_statfs_reply(), handle_get_version_reply() and handle_auth_reply(). A well-formed ack has front.iov_len >= 22 and is unaffected; a short one takes the existing bad: path. This applies commit d3c32939fa0e ("libceph: bound get_version reply decode to front len") to the last decode-side use of front_alloc_len in this file.

t: netfilter: nft_fwd_netdev: use recursion counter in neigh egress path
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: nft_fwd_netdev: use recursion counter in neigh egress path nft_fwd_neigh can be used in egress chains (NF_NETDEV_EGRESS). When the forwarding rule targets the same device or two devices forward to each other, neigh_xmit() triggers dev_queue_xmit() which re-enters nf_hook_egress(), causing infinite recursion and stack overflow. Move the nf_get_nf_dup_skb_recursion() accessor and NF_RECURSION_LIMIT to the shared header nf_dup_netdev.h as a static inline, so that nft_fwd_netdev can use the recursion counter directly without exported function call overhead. Guard neigh_xmit() with the same recursion limit already used in nf_do_netdev_egress(). [ Updated to cache the nf_get_nf_dup_skb_recursion pointer. --pablo ]

t: fuse: don't BUG when the copy buffer is exhausted
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: fuse: don't BUG when the copy buffer is exhausted fuse_copy_fill() hits BUG_ON(!err) once the iterator backing the copy runs out of pages. Over io-uring the amount copied is not bounded by the payload buffer the server registered, so an unprivileged user can drain the iterator and panic the host - mount a FUSE filesystem with small payload buffers, then setxattr() a larger value: kernel BUG at fs/fuse/dev.c:1064! Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 148 Comm: exploit Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1 #2 RIP: 0010:fuse_copy_fill (fs/fuse/dev.c:1033) Call Trace: <TASK> fuse_copy_args (fs/fuse/dev.c:1354 fs/fuse/dev.c:1380) fuse_uring_args_to_ring (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:891) fuse_uring_prepare_send (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:940 fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:1057) fuse_uring_send_in_task (fs/fuse/dev_uring.c:1745) tctx_task_work_run (io_uring/tw.c:96) tctx_task_work (io_uring/tw.c:133) task_work_run (kernel/task_work.c:233) io_run_task_work (io_uring/tw.h:84) io_cqring_wait (io_uring/wait.c:278) __do_sys_io_uring_enter (io_uring/io_uring.c:2676) do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61) entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121) The reply path can drain it the same way, via the server-supplied payload_sz in fuse_uring_copy_from_ring(). Return -EIO instead. All three fuse_copy_fill() callers already propagate the error.

t: smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl() In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or 5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) on posix). However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() -> copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total), and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes) even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past the end of the slab buffer. Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

t: ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() uses the MAX_CIFS_SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE (448-byte) buffer for a single SMB2_CREATE response. That buffer also holds a 4-byte length field, which only leaves 444 bytes for the SMB2 body. The AAPL response made this buffer too small. After 8f1b796ff113, a request with AAPL response contexts may need at least 456 bytes. In the 456-byte case, create_aapl_rsp_buf() is appended last, clears 128 bytes, and writes 12 bytes past the allocation. KASAN reports: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0 Write of size 128 at addr ffff88800370954c by task kworker/0:0/9 ... create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0 smb2_open+0x58f9/0xef10 ... smb2_allocate_rsp_buf+0x19d/0x370 ... The buggy address is located 332 bytes inside of allocated 448-byte region [ffff888003709400, ffff8880037095c0) Reserve enough space for any fixed CREATE response KSMBD can build. Store the required allocation size in the per-dialect values table. This keeps the small buffer for other commands and avoids using the max transaction buffer for every CREATE.

t: ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry. If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to remove the volatile id. Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops its references first, the other request makes the final put through ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed memory. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd] Call Trace: __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd] ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd] ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd] ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd] ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd] Freed by task 1030: __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd] smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd] Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not one made by another holder. Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path, before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

t: ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF
d: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id() supersedes a prior open that has the same AppInstanceId. It reaches that open's session through opinfo->sess. This pointer is not refcounted. Session teardown detaches durable handles before it frees the session. It does not detach a non-durable open. That open still points at the session through opinfo->sess after the session is freed. Another session can supersede the open at the same time. The supersede then takes a write lock through the stale pointer, in the freed session's file table. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0 Call Trace: _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0 ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id+0xd9/0x670 [ksmbd] smb2_open+0x3e10/0xd910 [ksmbd] Freed by task 212: ksmbd_session_destroy+0x38d/0x480 [ksmbd] Fix this by looking the session up by opinfo->session_id. The lookup returns a reference, as smb2_break_collect_channels() does. Recheck that opinfo->sess still points at it before using it. Do the lookup without m_lock held. destroy_previous_session() takes m_lock under the session table lock, and taking them in the other order here would deadlock.

t: Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message
d: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.

A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. Exploitation requires user interaction, specifically opening a specially crafted file, which then causes the application to traverse outside the target directory and to write files in unauthorized locations, eventually enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE). This can lead to a complete compromise of the system running Rexroth IndraWorks.

t: Apache Griffin Web Service: REST API is unauthenticated
d: ** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Apache Griffin Web Service. The REST API does not have any authentication. This includes sensitive endpoints, such as job submission when a Livy/Spark backend is configured. The API must be properly secured on the network level, and this fact was arguably not documented as clearly as it could have. This issue affects Apache Griffin Web Service: all versions. As this project is retired, we do not plan to release a version that fixes this issue. Users are recommended to find an alternative or restrict access to the instance to trusted users. NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

t: vulnerability-lookup: Session Persists After Password Change (CWE-613)
d: In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the Flask-Login session identifier was set to the bare numeric user ID (User.get_id() returned self.id). Because the session ID contained no component derived from the user's credential, it remained valid indefinitely regardless of any subsequent password change, account recovery, or administrator-initiated password reset. An attacker who had obtained a valid session for a user account (for example through cross-site scripting, session hijacking, or a previously exposed feed or API key) could continue to access that user's account after the user changed their password, because the session cookie still carried the same static user ID and the user_loader accepted it without any credential-bound validation. The affected component is the session management layer of the vulnerability-lookup Flask application, specifically the User.get_id() method in website/models/user.py and the load_user callback in website/web/views/session_mgmt.py. The vulnerability required that an attacker already possessed a valid session for the target user; no additional authentication or special deployment configuration was needed beyond a standard deployment of the application. The security impact is that a user cannot effectively revoke an attacker's access by changing their password, performing an account recovery, or having an administrator reset the credential. The attacker retains full authenticated access to the user's profile, subscriptions, and any role-gated functionality for the lifetime of the session cookie. Additionally, sessions that were opened via a feed key or API key before a prior fix (commit 3605d5b6) also persisted indefinitely.

t: vulnerability-lookup: Feed key or API key authentication creates full web session bypassing password and 2FA
d: In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators.py) and API-key requests (auth_func in website/web/api/v1/common.py) called Flask-Login's login_user() function. This caused the HTTP response to a request authenticated solely by a feed key (supplied as the X-FEED-KEY URL parameter) or an API key (supplied as the X-API-KEY header) to set a session cookie that grants full authenticated access to every page in the application, without requiring a password or two-factor authentication. The practical impact is that any party possessing a leaked feed URL (a common occurrence, as feed URLs are shared with RSS readers) or an API key could obtain a valid web session for the associated account. This session provides access to the user's account page, which exposes the API key and other profile data, and for accounts with the administrator role, access to the /admin interface, enabling full administrative control of the application. The vulnerability affects all users whose feed key or API key is exposed. No prior authentication, user interaction, or special network conditions are required; a single HTTP request with the token is sufficient to establish the session. The session persists until it expires, and because it is not bound to the original credential (a related CWE-613 issue noted by the developers), revoking the feed key or API key does not invalidate the already-created session. The fix replaces the login_user() call with assignment to g._login_user, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads for the current request only, without writing any session cookie. The affected views remain unchanged and continue to see the authenticated user for the single request.

t: Burst Statistics < 3.7.5 - Unauthenticated Plugin Load Suppression via Crafted Request Path
d: The Burst Statistics WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not verify that a request is actually being routed to its own REST API before unloading every other active plugin for that request, allowing unauthenticated attackers to have requests processed with other plugins' protections (such as REST access restrictions, hidden login pages and two-factor authentication) switched off, and to cause other plugins' scheduled tasks to be discarded.

t: Kadence Memberships < 4.0.6 - Unauthenticated Paid Membership Activation Without Payment via Renewal Level Mismatch
d: The Kadence Memberships WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not check that the membership level submitted when renewing a membership matches the level being renewed, pricing the renewal from the submitted level while activating the membership at its own level, allowing unauthenticated users to activate a paid membership without paying on sites that also offer a free level.

t: Denial of service vulnerability in QXmlSimpleReader impacts Qt
d: A denial of service vulnerability in the Qt QXmlSimpleReader class of the Qt 5 Core Compatibility APIs module (Qt 6) and the Qt XML module (Qt 5).

t: Social Viral Downloader <= 2.0.3 - Unauthenticated Download Log Deletion
d: The Social Viral Downloader WordPress plugin through 2.0.3 does not have authorisation or nonce checks on a log deletion action available to unauthenticated users, which could allow them to delete the Social Viral Downloader WordPress plugin through 2.0.3's entire download log.

t: Social Viral Downloader <= 2.0.3 - Unauthenticated Download Log Disclosure
d: The Social Viral Downloader WordPress plugin through 2.0.3 does not have authorisation or nonce checks on a log export action available to unauthenticated users, which could allow them to export the download log, including registered users' email addresses and IP addresses, to a publicly accessible file.

t: Out-of-bounds write in HOTP trusted application of Samsung Open Source mTower
d: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source mTower allows Overflow Buffers.

Dell PowerStore contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. A low-privileged authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to execution of malicious script in a higher-privileged user's session.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization-bypass vulnerability. A low-privileged attacker could exploit it, potentially leading to elevation of privilege to administrator.

t: Type confusion in overloaded Web IDL binding resolution in Samsung Starfish allows remote web content to cause memory corruption via WebGL bufferData()
d: Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Input Data Manipulation.

t: Improper access control in file: URL handling in Samsung Starfish allows remote web content to read local files
d: Files or directories accessible to external parties vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Probe System Files.

t: SSCMS 7.2.0 through 7.4.0 Arbitrary File Read via layerImageUpload Endpoint
d: SSCMS 7.2.0 through 7.4.0 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any registered user-center account to copy server files by supplying source paths to the layerImageUpload endpoint. Attackers can send siteId 0 with crafted filePaths entries to copy configuration files into their public sitefiles/home upload directory and download them anonymously.

t: EdgeChat 2.5.0 through 2.21.0 XSS via @-Mention Autocomplete Username
d: EdgeChat 2.5.0 through 2.21.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows invited users to inject HTML through unescaped usernames in the Vditor @-mention autocomplete. Attackers can register with a username containing an img onerror payload that executes when mentioned, stealing the localStorage session token to take over victim accounts.

t: VoAPI 1.0.0 through 1.2.0 SQL Injection via search Filter Key
d: VoAPI 1.0.0 through 1.2.0 contains a sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject SQL by supplying crafted column names as search[...] filter keys on list endpoints such as GET /api/log. Attackers can read the HS256 JWT signing secret from the option table and forge a manager role token to take over the /api/m/* management API.

t: Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through 63152c4 Stored XSS via Comment Reply Dialog
d: Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through commit 63152c4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by posting unsanitized comment content rendered via jQuery .html() in the reply dialog. Attackers can post comments with img onerror payloads that execute when victims click Reply, stealing the non-HttpOnly sid session cookie to hijack accounts including administrators.

t: Bolo (bolo-solo) 1.7 through 2.6.4 Stored XSS via Comment Reply-To Name
d: Bolo (bolo-solo) 1.7 through 2.6.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts via the unsanitized commentOriginalCommentName parameter. Attackers can post a comment to /article/comments with a short payload that steals non-HttpOnly session cookies from visitors, enabling takeover of administrator accounts.

t: Bolo (bolo-solo) 1.7 through 2.6.4 Article Password Disclosure via /articles
d: Bolo (bolo-solo) 1.7 through 2.6.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read article view passwords via the public GET /articles endpoint. Attackers can retrieve the plaintext articleViewPwd field returned by ArticleProcessor.getArticlesByPage and submit it to read password-protected article content.

t: CloudPaste 1.1.0 through 1.9.1 WebDAV Credential Disclosure via /api/proxy/link
d: CloudPaste 1.1.0 through 1.9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain WebDAV storage credentials through the unauthenticated /api/proxy/link endpoint. Attackers who know a public share slug can retrieve the Basic Authorization header containing the WebDAV username and password, then read, modify, or delete files on the WebDAV server.

t: Gitea pull request disclosure to members with access to issues only
d: Several endpoints that work on both issues and pull requests did not check which of the two the addressed item is. A user who can read a repository's issues but not its pull requests could read pull request data through the issue sub-resources of the API (timeline, attachments, labels, subscriptions, tracked times and reactions), and list pull requests through the repository's issue search and milestone pages; the same applied in the other direction. These endpoints now check read access to the unit the item belongs to. The API endpoints were fixed in 28.2.0 and 28.3.0, the search and milestone pages in 28.4.0.

t: Gitea release asset deletion by former writers
d: The web endpoint that removes an attachment skipped the permission check when the request came from the user who had uploaded the attachment, and it was reachable with read access to issues or pull requests. A user who had uploaded a release asset could still delete it after losing write access to the repository. The endpoint now only deletes attachments that the user uploaded and that are not yet linked to an issue, comment or release.

t: Gitea push without write access to repositories still being created
d: Git over HTTP lowers the required permission for pushes to read access, so that the AGit flow works, and relies on the repository's server-side hooks to enforce write access. A repository that is still being created by a migration, fork or template generation has no hooks yet, so a user with read access to it could push branches and tags during that window, or after a failed migration that left the repository in that state. Git over HTTP now refuses requests to repositories that are still being created.

t: Gitea required approval bypass through team review request removal
d: Removing a team's review request looked up a review by the negated team ID, which for the team with ID 2 is the ID of the built-in Actions user, and marked the review it found as official. In the organization that owns that team, a user who can change the review requests of a pull request could make an approval left by the Actions user count toward the approvals required by branch protection. Merging still required permission to merge. Removing a team review request no longer changes any review.

t: Gitea OAuth2 provider tokens issued to disabled users
d: When Gitea acts as an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider, the token endpoint did not check the state of the user. After an administrator deactivated an account or prohibited its sign-in, existing refresh tokens and unused authorization codes of that user could still be exchanged for new tokens, so applications that sign users in through Gitea kept them signed in. The token endpoint now refuses users who may not sign in, and token introspection reports their tokens as inactive.

t: Gitea disclosure of pending pull request reviews created through the API
d: A pull request review created through the API as a draft (`event` set to `PENDING` or left empty) was added to the pull request timeline and announced through notifications and activity feeds like a submitted review. Its body and line comments were therefore visible to everyone who can read the pull request, including anonymous visitors of a public repository, before the reviewer submitted it. Pending reviews no longer get a timeline entry or notifications until they are submitted.

t: Gitea private diff disclosure through code comment replies
d: Replying to a code review comment accepted a review ID that belongs to a different pull request, through the web form, the API and incoming mail replies. A signed-in user could reply on a pull request they can access with the ID of a review in a repository they cannot read, and the new comment was attached to that review and received the diff context of the commented lines. Replies are now only accepted for a review of the same pull request, and for a pending review only from its author.

t: Gitea hidden organization membership disclosure through the permissions API
d: `GET /api/v1/users/{username}/orgs/{org}/permissions` only checked that the organization is visible to the caller and then returned the named user's role in it. Any signed-in user could learn whether another user is an owner, admin or member of a public or limited organization, including for members who conceal their membership. The roles are now only returned to the user themselves, to members of the organization and to site administrators.

t: Gitea pull request creation without pull request access through AGit
d: The AGit flow (pushing to `refs/for/...`) did not check the pusher's access to pull requests again when it created the pull request. A user or deploy key with read access to the code only, or with write access to the wiki over SSH, could open pull requests in a repository where they have no access to pull requests. Creating a pull request through AGit now requires read access to the pull requests of the repository and is refused for wiki pushes.

t: Gitea protected file pattern bypass with quoted file names
d: The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path.

t: Gitea deletion of arbitrary attachment files through release edit
d: When a release was edited, the files of the attachments to remove were deleted by the identifiers submitted in the form rather than by the attachments verified to belong to the release. A user with write access to the releases of any repository, including their own, could submit a crafted identifier that resolves to the stored file of another attachment and delete it, provided they know that attachment's UUID. The attachment record stayed, so downloads of the affected issue, comment or release file failed. Release edits now only delete the files of attachments that belong to the release.

t: Gitea base repository code disclosure through the web editor in forks
d: When a file is edited in a fork through the web editor, Gitea can first copy a branch from the base repository into the fork. That copy did not check whether the user may read the base repository's code. A user who had forked a repository and later lost access to it, for example after it was made private or they were removed as a collaborator, could keep copying its current branches into their fork and read them. The copy now requires read access to the code of the base repository.

t: Gitea missing attempt limit for TOTP passcodes
d: Gitea accepted an unlimited number of wrong TOTP passcodes during sign-in, in the password reset flow and for Basic authentication with the `X-Gitea-OTP` header. An attacker who already knows an account's password could guess the six-digit passcode by trying codes at a high rate and sign in despite two-factor authentication. After five failed passcodes, further attempts for the account are now refused for 15 minutes.

t: Gitea deletion of shared container blobs on rejected uploads
d: When a container blob upload was rejected, for example because it exceeded a package size quota, the cleanup removed the blob from storage even if the same content already existed and was used by other packages. On an instance with a package quota configured, a user who can upload container images and has the exact content of another owner's package file or image layer could make it undownloadable. The cleanup now only removes blobs that the failed upload created.

t: Gitea stored cross-site scripting in the issue reference popup
d: The popup shown when hovering an issue reference loaded its data from the path of the hovered link and inserted part of the response as HTML. A user who can post a comment or other rendered content could add a link that is displayed as an ordinary issue reference but points to a file in a repository they control, so that the popup inserted that file's content into the page of anyone hovering the link and ran script in the viewer's session. The popup now requests the issue by the owner, repository and index parsed from the link.

t: Gitea anonymous Git LFS access despite required sign-in
d: With `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW = true`, the Git LFS endpoints still answered unauthenticated requests for repositories that are not private. An anonymous client who knows the path of such a repository and the SHA-256 of an LFS object could download the object, and could use the batch endpoint to test whether an object exists. The Git LFS endpoints now require authentication when sign-in is required to view the instance.

t: Gitea scoped workflow trust kept after repository transfer
d: A repository registered by its owner as a source of scoped workflows kept that registration when it was transferred to another owner. The new owner could then change the workflows in the transferred repository, and they kept running in the previous owner's repositories with access to their Actions secrets and job tokens. A transfer now removes the owner-level registrations of the repository, and registrations whose source repository no longer belongs to the registering owner are ignored.

t: Gitea RubyGems compact index injection through package metadata
d: The RubyGems package registry accepted gems whose platform, dependency names or dependency version requirements contain newline characters. Because the compact index served to clients is line-based, a user who can publish a gem to an owner's registry could forge index entries, such as packages that do not exist or additional versions of an existing gem with dependencies of their choice. Clients that resolve gems from that registry could then be led to install attacker-chosen dependencies. Gems with such metadata are now rejected.

t: Gitea command execution through repository auto-initialization
d: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already contained. A user who is allowed to create repositories could push a crafted tree during that window so that writing the README followed a symbolic link and overwrote a server-side git hook, which runs commands as the Gitea system user. The initial commit is now built in a freshly initialized directory, and a new repository only becomes ready, and accepts pushes, once its initialization is complete.

t: Gitea password hash disclosure through repository search
d: The repository search used by the dashboard (`GET /repo/search`) returned the internal commit status object of each repository. Since 28.0.0 that object included the repository owner's full user record, so any signed-in user could read the password hash, salt and email address of the owner of any repository they can see that has a commit status. The response now contains only the state and target URL of the commit status.
